sentences.text: Today we will talk about Tallinn.
Tallinn is the capital city of Estonia.
It is a beautiful city on the coast of the Baltic Sea.
Tallinn is famous for its old town, colorful buildings and history.
The city is small but full of life.
People enjoy walking on the old streets and looking at old towers.
Let's explore Tallinn together and learn more about this amazing city.
Part two.
Where is Tallinn?
Tallinn is in northern Europe.
It is on the northern coast of Estonia.
It is near the sea and many ships and ferries arrive from Finland and Sweden.
The city is surrounded by forests and parks.
The air is fresh and clean.
Tallinn is an important city for business, tourism and culture in Estonia.
Part three.
A short history of Tallinn.
Tallinn is very old.
It was first mentioned over 800 years ago.
In the past it was part of Denmark, Sweden and Russia.
People built walls and towers to protect the city.
The old town of Tallinn is very well preserved.
It has cobblestone streets, churches and houses from the Middle Ages.
Today Tallinn is modern but still keeps its history alive.
Part four.
Tallinn Old Town.
The old town is the most famous part of Tallinn.
It has narrow streets, old houses and big walls.
The streets are full of shops, cafes and restaurants.
One famous place is Town Hall Square where people meet and celebrate festivals.
Walking in the old town feels like going back in time.
Part five.
Tallinn Landmarks.
Tallinn has many landmarks.
One is Tumpia Castle, a big castle on a hill.
Now it is the government building.
Another is Alexander Nefsky Cathedral, a beautiful church with big golden domes.
You can also visit St.
Olaf's Church which was once the tallest building in the world.
These landmarks show the history and culture of Tallinn.
Part six.
Nature around Tallinn.
Nature is very close to Tallinn.
There are parks, forests and beaches near the city.
People enjoy walking, cycling and relaxing in nature.
One famous park is Kadriorg Park with beautiful gardens and a palace.
Tallinn is a city where people can enjoy both history and nature.
Part seven.
Festivals in Tallinn.
Tallinn has many festivals every year.
One famous festival is the Tallinn Old Town Days where people celebrate history with music, dance and food.
There is also the Tallinn Music Week with concerts from many countries.
During Christmas, the Christmas market in the town square is very popular.
Festivals bring people together and make the city lively.
Part eight.
Food in Tallinn.
Food in Tallinn is tasty and simple.
People eat fish, potatoes, bread and vegetables.
One famous dish is black bread with smoked fish.
Other traditional foods include soup with meat or vegetables and mulled wine in winter.
There are also many international restaurants in Tallinn with Italian, Asian and French food.
Food is important in Tallinn, especially when meeting family and friends.
Part nine.
People of Tallinn.
People in Tallinn are friendly, polite and helpful.
Many people speak English, especially younger people.
They enjoy music, art and spending time outdoors.
Family is very important and people often meet in cafes, parks or at home.
The culture of Tallinn is a mix of old traditions and modern life.
Part 10.
Weather in Tallinn.
The weather in Tallinn is cold in winter and mild in summer.
Winter is snowy and dark, but the city looks magical with lights and decorations.
Summer is sunny and warm and people enjoy walking, cycling and sitting outside.
Spring and autumn are beautiful with flowers and colorful leaves.
Tallinn is special in every season.
Part 11.
Technology and modern life.
Tallinn is very modern and digital.
It is one of the smartest cities in the world.
People use technology for banking, government and education.
There are many cafes, shops and co -working spaces with computers and internet.
Even though it is modern, Tallinn still keeps its history alive in old streets and buildings.
Part 12.
Goodbye from Tallinn.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English podcast.
I am Emily.
Tallinn is a city of history, culture and nature.
You can walk on old streets, visit castles, eat tasty food and enjoy the parks and sea.
It is a city where the past and present live together.
I hope you can visit Tallinn one day and see its beauty with your own eyes.
